name: David Whitmer
role: One of the Three Witnesses of the Book of Mormon
dateNote: He was baptized in June 1829, and the revelations to him in sections 14 and 18 date from that month.
importance: In June 1829 David Whitmer moved Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery from Harmony to his father’s farm in Fayette. Section 14 calls him “to assist,” and section 18 tells him and Oliver to search out the Twelve. He became one of the Three Witnesses; section 30 rebukes him for fearing man, and section 52 sends him to Missouri. He later led the Church in Missouri, was excommunicated in 1838, and kept affirming his witness.
connections: He was a son of Peter Whitmer Sr.; his brothers John, Peter Jr., and Christian also joined, and his sister Elizabeth married Oliver Cowdery. Section 52 pairs him with Harvey Whitlock.

sources.title: David Whitmer, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Dates, baptism, Missouri presidency (1834), rejection (Feb. 1838) and excommunication (13 Apr. 1838) checked on JSP. Bare “David” is left out because it also names King David (124, 132). The 1887 Address affirming his witness is on the JSP page.
